unresolved.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of Pyridazine Salts under Batch and Flow
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report an [Ir(COD)Cl]2/(R)-SunPhos-catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of pyridazine salts to construct chiral hexahydropyridazines. The reaction tolerates a wide range of substituents, delivering products in up to 97% yield with 97% ee under mild reaction conditions. Simultaneously, the gram-scale synthesis, continuous-flow operation, and good catalyst turnover (TON up to 3720 with 94% ee at S/C = 4000; TOF up to 155 h–1) further underscored the practicality of this methodology. Collectively, this operationally simple, scalable, and sustainable protocol provides an efficient platform for valuable N-heterocycles featuring chiral hexahydropyridazine cores.

Nature controls reactivity through precisely organized secondary coordination spheres. Inspired by this principle, symmetry remodelling of a urea-functionalized iron porphyrin creates directional hydrogen-bonding interactions that enable unprecedented CO2 reduction in aprotic media and boost catalysis in the presence of a proton source. Optimal catalysis thus arises not only from intermediate stabilization but also from adaptive, directional non-covalent interactions. A Charge-Enhanced Hydrogen Bonding Strategy for Halogen Bond Activation in Catalysis
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Catalysis underpins modern chemical innovation, yet halogen-bond catalysts remain underdeveloped. Herein, we introduce a charged hydrogen bond-enhanced halogen bond (HBeXB) platform that intensifies σ-hole electrophilicity to unlock reactivity. Mechanistic, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a cooperative network of hydrogen bonding, halogen bonding, and nonclassical C–H interactions, delivering exceptional catalytic rates. The modular design of these scaffolds establishes a broadly applicable strategy for next generation organocatalysis.

unresolved.title: Synthesis of Diaryl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Derivatives via Three-Component Reactions of o -Quinone Diimides with Alcohols and Diazo Compounds
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Highly regioselective three-component reactions of o-quinone diimides with alcohols and diazo compounds have been developed with a rhodium catalyst. This transformation is proposed to proceed through a Michael-type trapping of oxonium ylide intermediates with arylation reagents, giving access to a range of diaryl α-hydroxycarboxylic acid derivatives bearing an oxa-quaternary center in good yields. This reaction featured broad substrate scope, scale-up synthesis, and late-stage functionalization of the complex molecule.

unresolved.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

unresolved.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
unresolved.abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

unresolved.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
unresolved.abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change. unresolved.title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
unresolved.abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. unresolved.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
unresolved.abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.
